articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: The Overseer is an interface role rather than a fixed person with a franchise-wide biography. Players choose a Vault number, assign rooms and direct a population through an open-ended management simulation.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Objectives include maintaining resources, admitting dwellers, responding to incidents and sending teams into the wasteland. These systems demonstrate Vault life themes without establishing one historical facility.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: The archive scopes this record to Fallout Shelter's gameplay-forward supplementary continuity. Random incidents, crossover characters and repeated quests are not promoted into unconditional world chronology.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: A Shelter Vault begins as a small underground facility and expands through rooms for power, food, water, training, production and habitation. Layout and Vault number are player-selected.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Dwellers work, form families, explore and respond to attacks or accidents under the Overseer's direction. The simulation combines recognisable franchise institutions with balance-driven mechanics.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: No one layout, population or disaster sequence is treated as a canonical Vault history. The record exists to index the game's central subject while maintaining source boundaries.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: Dwellers have names, SPECIAL attributes, equipment and work assignments generated or selected within the simulation. Some resemble characters from other Fallout works through collection systems.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Population growth and expeditions give the Vault a continuing social loop, but repetition and random generation mean these residents do not form one stable historical cast.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: Named crossover appearances are therefore metadata about the game, not evidence that every represented character cohabited one Vault at one time.

summary: The archival continuity rule separating Fallout Shelter's management systems from unconditional franchise history.
description: The archival continuity rule separating Fallout Shelter's management systems from unconditional franchise history.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: Fallout Shelter presents Vault-Tec architecture, creatures, equipment and people through a repeatable mobile-management structure. That structure is useful reference material but is not a conventional fixed campaign.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: The archive can index what the game depicts while qualifying randomly generated rooms, incidents and cross-title character collection. This prevents gameplay convenience from becoming false chronology.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: Future records should cite fixed quest text or official material where available and retain this scope for simulation-only claims.
